questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Nature, language (close to danish), possibility of sustainable travel

questions.answer: Quite easy. Helps to be in contact with other students.

questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Fantoft is fine but impersonal, would prefer to live in the city.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Fantoft is very large, you live with other exchange students. Can be fine if its what youre after.

questions.answer: Dont remember, sorry.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Succesful, but others were not. Complications can arise if specific courses are needed, but that is a general problem with erasmus.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you want to be 100p sure to get the course, maybe contact the course responsible to ask if you satisfy the needed restrictions, especially on math/nat science.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: On Physics and Geophysics, the levels are medium-high, stimulating but could be more challenging at times. Theoretical physics courses differed a lot in level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: About the same, but physics department is small, so the teams are small and exams oral.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
GEOF213
PHYS203
PHYS261

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: PHYS203 and GEOF213 teach you a lot. Geophysics is a "specialty" at Bergen with a lot of nice local students, try it out if you can. Geography students may have a hard time applying, i succeded as a physics student.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some cool climate-groups in Bergen.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Lots of sports clubs, political institutions etc. There is a open hall-event in the beginning of the semester for all.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Engage politically or in sports, or in particular in nature-related events.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hike around the city, its great and cheap. Bring boots and raincoats.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy as a danish person. Language needs to adjust but its ok.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Scandinavian language helps! If not sport clubs, volunteering in student bars or in climate groups like Spire or Stop Oljeletinga.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Weather can be difficult at times, though it is beautiful when it clears out. The norwegians can be reserved, but also very warming and nice when you get close to them.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Culture around the nature.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Bring hiking gear if you like that stuff!
It may rain a lot, but when it is nice (which it also is sometimes!) skip school and go swim or hike, life is more than books.
If you are a person who is generally a lot happier in the sun, maybe go more south. But if you choose Bergen like me, there is so much to enjoy. Nowhere is the nature as beautiful as in Norway, and you will see it if you let it.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dont know.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Friends I met through Geophysics in Bergen, some tough courses i completed and am proud of, and winter swimming in the fjords.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Allowing myself to spend more time with myself.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
